chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir from Harun ibn Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'When you fast for the sighting of the crescent and break your fast for its sighting, you have completed the fasting of the month, even if you did not fast except for twenty-nine days. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The month is like this, like this, and like this,
and he gestured with his hand to ten, ten, and nine.
ai.seo_question: Is fasting for 29 days sufficient to complete Ramadan if the moon is not seen on the 30th day?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the lunar calendar mechanics by affirming that a month of fasting is complete with either twenty-nine or thirty days, depending on the sighting of the crescent. It highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practical demonstration of variable month lengths, a principle foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding the determination of Eid al-Fitr. This ruling ensures the validity of the fast even if the month falls short of thirty days, emphasizing reliance on actual observation over fixed numerical assumptions.
